title: Archon — System Overview
purpose: Understand Archon's mission, architecture, evidence posture, and explicit boundaries.
limitations: This is derivative learning material, not canonical implementation evidence.
Archon is verified as a local base seven-service system with an optional eighth Jaeger service; no public or cloud deployment is claimed.
Counts and acceptance status must be rechecked against the source commit and canonical evidence documents.

concepts.label: Reliability Workbench
concepts.summary: Archon is a local control plane for governing and inspecting agent runs, not merely a chat screen.

teaching.definition: The Agent Reliability Workbench is the product boundary that joins an authenticated SvelteKit interface to a FastAPI control plane and an evidence-producing runtime.
teaching.responsibility: Present one coherent surface for starting bounded runs, approving sensitive actions, inspecting evidence, and reviewing evaluations.
controls: Visible distinction between answers and evidence
teaching.failure_behavior: If authentication or dependencies are unavailable, protected operations fail rather than silently becoming anonymous or mock success.
teaching.why_it_matters: The UI is useful only because deterministic backend controls and durable evidence sit behind it; appearance alone is not reliability.

concepts.boundary: A local workbench does not establish public deployment, production traffic, or an SLO.
concepts.narration: Archon is a local Agent Reliability Workbench. Its interface starts and inspects runs, but reliability comes from the typed control plane, deterministic governance, and durable evidence behind the screen.
concepts.scenario: A reviewer sees a polished chat interface and asks what makes Archon more than an LLM wrapper.
options: The governed runtime, evidence, and evaluation lifecycle
concepts.scenario_explanation: The differentiator is the explicit control and evidence lifecycle, not presentation or an unclaimed deployment.

concepts.label: Loopback Gateway
concepts.summary: An unprivileged Nginx gateway is the only service that publishes a host port in the verified target.

teaching.definition: The gateway is the loopback entry boundary that routes browser traffic to the frontend or backend while keeping dependency services off host ports.
teaching.responsibility: Route traffic to the correct internal service without exposing PostgreSQL, Redis, OTEL, backend, frontend, or sandbox ports directly.
teaching.failure_behavior: An unavailable upstream yields a gateway failure; it does not bypass the service boundary or expose internal ports.
teaching.why_it_matters: One narrow entry point reduces accidental exposure and makes health and routing behavior easier to verify.

concepts.boundary: Loopback isolation is not Internet-edge hardening, TLS, WAF, or public ingress evidence.
concepts.narration: The verified target exposes one loopback gateway. The application and data services remain internal, which narrows accidental host exposure without pretending to be a hardened public edge.
concepts.scenario: An operator proposes publishing PostgreSQL directly so local debugging is easier.
options: Keep it internal and use managed operational paths
Call direct exposure a readiness check
concepts.scenario_explanation: The verified architecture intentionally exposes only the loopback gateway.

concepts.label: SvelteKit Workbench
concepts.summary: The frontend provides authenticated chat, approvals, evidence inspection, settings, and learning views.

teaching.definition: The SvelteKit Workbench is the user-facing projection of runtime state and durable records.
teaching.responsibility: Render answer-first workflows while preserving access to policy decisions, tool activity, evidence, evaluations, and learning artifacts.
teaching.failure_behavior: Expired authentication redirects to login; transient SSE loss must not be confused with deletion of durable run records.
teaching.why_it_matters: A reliable system must make controls and evidence usable, not merely store them in backend tables.

concepts.boundary: SSE is a transient projection; the frontend is not the authoritative Run Ledger.
concepts.narration: SvelteKit turns durable controls into usable workflows: chat, approvals, evidence, evaluation, and learning. Streaming progress is transient; durable records remain authoritative.
concepts.scenario: The browser loses an SSE connection after a tool result was persisted.
concepts.scenario_explanation: Transient streaming and durable persistence are separate boundaries.

concepts.label: FastAPI Control Plane
concepts.summary: FastAPI authenticates requests, wires scoped dependencies, and exposes runtime and evidence APIs.

teaching.definition: The FastAPI service is the application control plane that validates identity and input before constructing request-scoped runtime dependencies.
teaching.responsibility: Bind persistence, provider, policy, approval, tools, events, and observability into the correct route path.
teaching.failure_behavior: Invalid identity, scope, configuration, or dependencies stop the request with an explicit error rather than continuing with weaker controls.
teaching.why_it_matters: Correct dependency wiring is where architecture becomes an exercised product path rather than disconnected classes.

concepts.boundary: Route existence is not proof that every optional capability is enabled or observed.
concepts.narration: FastAPI is the control-plane entry. It authenticates and scopes requests, then constructs the provider, policy, approval, tool, event, and persistence boundaries used by the runtime.
concepts.scenario: A new SSE route constructs its own runtime without the shared policy-aware factory.
options: Route it through the shared preparation and factory path
Trust the model to enforce policy
concepts.scenario_explanation: Sync and SSE must share governed construction so behavior does not drift.

concepts.label: Typed AgentRuntime
concepts.summary: A custom Protocol-based runtime owns bounded model/tool transitions and explicit stop reasons.

teaching.definition: AgentRuntime is a typed, provider-neutral interpreter around a probabilistic model, not an agent framework abstraction that owns hidden control flow.
teaching.responsibility: Advance model and tool turns while enforcing iteration, token, tool-call, time, and monetary boundaries.
controls: Model output has no direct execution authority
Every terminal path is represented explicitly
teaching.failure_behavior: Provider, budget, validation, policy, approval, or tool failures terminate or return governed feedback according to typed rules.
teaching.why_it_matters: The runtime makes stopping, authority, and evidence reviewable instead of burying them inside model behavior.

concepts.boundary: Protocol-based portability does not prove identical behavior across every provider.
concepts.narration: AgentRuntime is the bounded interpreter around the model. It owns transitions and limits; the model supplies text or intent but cannot grant itself authority.
concepts.scenario: The model asks for a twenty-first tool call after the configured maximum is reached.
options: Execute because the model requested it
Stop with the configured tool-budget behavior
concepts.scenario_explanation: Deterministic runtime limits, not model preference, control execution.

concepts.label: Policy and Approvals
concepts.summary: Deterministic policy returns ALLOW, ASK, or DENY; ASK requires an exact durable decision before execution.

teaching.definition: Governance is the deterministic authorization layer between model-proposed tool intent and an effect.
receives: Risk, resource, owner, project, run, and call scope
teaching.responsibility: Evaluate policy and, when ASK is returned, bind a single-use decision to the exact proposed operation.
teaching.failure_behavior: Unknown metadata, missing authorizer, expiry, mismatch, cancellation, and duplicate consumption fail closed.
teaching.why_it_matters: Typed tools are still dangerous unless authority is decided outside the probabilistic planner.

concepts.boundary: Local policy tests do not constitute an external security audit.
concepts.narration: Policy decides ALLOW, ASK, or DENY. ASK pauses before execution and binds approval to the exact user, run, call, tool, and arguments. The model cannot approve itself.
concepts.scenario: A call is approved, then one argument changes before dispatch.
options: Ask the model whether it is safe
Execute and update the ledger later
concepts.scenario_explanation: Approval applies only to the immutable operation that was reviewed.

concepts.label: Governed Execution
concepts.summary: Authorized native, MCP, or sandbox tools execute through bounded registries rather than directly from model output.

teaching.definition: Governed execution is the effect boundary where validated and authorized operations reach a registered handler, MCP adapter, or isolated sandbox.
teaching.responsibility: Execute only the approved operation and normalize success, error, timeout, and cancellation outcomes.
produces: Effect or idempotency evidence where applicable
teaching.failure_behavior: Unavailable, timed-out, denied, malformed, or mismatched operations remain explicit failures and do not become successful evidence.
teaching.why_it_matters: This boundary turns a proposal into a controlled effect without broadening its authority.

concepts.boundary: Container isolation is local and not VM-grade hostile multi-tenant certification.
concepts.narration: Only validated and authorized calls reach native tools, governed MCP, or the networkless sandbox. Failures remain typed outcomes; isolation is strong local evidence, not a universal security certificate.
concepts.scenario: The sandbox service is unavailable for a code execution request.
options: Run the code on the host
Fail because there is no host fallback
Ask the model to simulate success
Record a successful result with no output
concepts.scenario_explanation: The verified design explicitly forbids host fallback.

concepts.label: Run Ledger
concepts.summary: Ordered owner-scoped events preserve a reconstructable control-flow history within documented redaction limits.

teaching.definition: The Run Ledger is an append-oriented domain record of run status and safe runtime events; it is not free-form logs or model memory.
receives: Policy, approval, model, tool, usage, and stop events
teaching.responsibility: Persist ordered evidence for inspection, stored-only replay, fork lineage, comparison, and later evaluation.
controls: Failed events are not rewritten as success
teaching.failure_behavior: Persistence failures are surfaced; missing evidence remains missing rather than reconstructed from a convenient final answer.
teaching.why_it_matters: Reliability analysis needs what actually happened, in order, not just what the assistant eventually said.

concepts.boundary: Replay reconstructs stored history and does not rerun models, tools, or arbitrary workspace state.
concepts.narration: The Run Ledger preserves ordered, scoped, redacted events and terminal state. It supports inspection and stored-only replay, but it is neither model memory nor executable resume.
concepts.scenario: A demo reloads a completed conversation and calls the result a replay.
options: Explain that stored-only replay reconstructs events
concepts.scenario_explanation: Archon's replay is historical reconstruction, not re-execution.

concepts.label: RAG and Evaluation
concepts.summary: Grounded document workflows and recorded-run evaluations use durable evidence but answer different questions.

teaching.definition: Knowledge and evaluation services retrieve scoped evidence, filter unsupported claims, and measure persisted trajectories through separate contracts.
receives: Completed run IDs and versioned fixtures
teaching.responsibility: Keep retrieval, grounding, bounded verification, and post-run evaluation distinct and inspectable.
teaching.failure_behavior: No evidence causes abstention; malformed or unsupported claims fail filtering; invalid evaluation identity fails validation.
teaching.why_it_matters: A final answer can look plausible while retrieval, support, citation, or evaluation evidence is weak.

concepts.boundary: Deterministic fixtures and one live sentinel do not establish broad model or retrieval quality.
concepts.narration: Archon stores embeddings as SQL JSON and computes cosine in Python. Grounding filters claims; recorded-run evaluation measures completed trajectories later. Neither should be renamed pgvector or general model-quality proof.
concepts.scenario: A report has citations but no claim-level support check.
options: Treat citation presence and correctness as separate
concepts.scenario_explanation: A marker can exist without supporting the attached claim.

concepts.label: Local Operations
concepts.summary: Seven retained services, readiness checks, CI, and recovery provide revision-scoped local operational evidence.

teaching.definition: Local operations is the reproducible target for building, migrating, checking dependencies, observing telemetry, and recovering Archon's durable state.
teaching.responsibility: Start and verify the base seven-service stack plus optional Jaeger profile, expose health versus readiness, and preserve or restore evidence safely.
controls: Managed wrapper owns retained stack state
teaching.failure_behavior: Failed readiness, migration, checksum, or clean-target checks block acceptance rather than being reported as PASS.
teaching.why_it_matters: Files and manifests are recipes; exercised readiness and recovery are the operational evidence.

concepts.boundary: One development-machine recovery observation is not an adopted production RTO or RPO objective.
concepts.narration: The local target has seven services and one gateway port. Health, readiness, migrations, telemetry, backup, and restore are exercised separately. These are local observations, never public deployment claims.
concepts.scenario: A Compose manifest exists, but no stack was started or probed.
concepts.scenario_explanation: A manifest is not a deployment or readiness observation.
